diagnostic_evidence.quote: According to the special structures of $(\star, \epsilon)$-palindromic matrix polynomial, we separate distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ and corresponding Jordan canonical form into the following two categories.

It is well known that the eigenvalues of the palindromic matrix polynomial $P(\lambda)$ always occur in pairs $(\lambda, 1/\lambda^{\star})$, or in quadruples $(\lambda, \bar{\lambda}, 1/{\lambda}, 1/{\bar{\lambda}})$ when $A$ and $Q$ are real

issues.failure_explanation: Case 2 asserts that every unit-circle eigenvalue of an (H,ε)-palindromic polynomial contributes a doubled Jordan group $\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_jI+N, \lambda_jI+N)$, i.e. that unit-circle eigenvalues have even algebraic multiplicity split into two identical halves. The reciprocity $\lambda\leftrightarrow 1/\lambda^\star$ is trivial on the unit circle ($1/\bar\lambda=\lambda$), so no structure forces a second copy: e.g. $P(\lambda)=\lambda^2+1$ ($n=1$, $A=1$, $Q=0$, $\star=H$, $\epsilon=1$, $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}$) has two simple eigenvalues $\pm\mathrm i$, and no standard pair $(X,J)$ with $J$ of the displayed doubled form exists, since a standard pair's $J$ must carry the true Jordan structure. Hence the H-case categories, and the Γ-structures built on them in Theorem thm-gamma-2 (display (gs-38)), Theorem thm-s-2 and the H-part of Corollary cor-1, are derived from a false classification and do not describe general H-palindromic polynomials.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Case 2's second category by single Jordan groups $\lambda_jI+N$ (self-paired unit-circle eigenvalues) and re-derive the corresponding Γ-block structure; the rest of the section and the applications carry over.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised characterization of the parameter matrix Γ for H-palindromic polynomials (contributions (ii), Section 3 Case 2, Theorems thm-gamma-2 and thm-s-2, H-part of cor-1) fails to cover any palindromic polynomial with a unit-circle eigenvalue of odd multiplicity (e.g. λ²+1); only the paper's main decomposition theorem (main-thm) and the T-case analysis survive.
issues.title: Case 2 (H-palindromic) Jordan classification wrongly doubles unit-circle eigenvalue blocks
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained re-derivation of the Γ-structure for the corrected unit-circle case (the pairing analysis becomes simpler), with no new global proof architecture; the central spectral decomposition, its applications and the T-case results are untouched, so a comparable version of the structure characterization survives.

issues.failure_explanation: For a cross-block $Z_{ik}$ ($i\neq k$) the defining equation $aZN_j^T+bN_jZ+N_jZN_j^T=0$ reads entrywise $az_{s,t+1}+bz_{s+1,t}+z_{s+1,t+1}=0$ (with out-of-range indices zero). For $n_i=3$, $n_k=2$ this forces $z_{22}=z_{31}=z_{32}=0$ and links $az_{12}+bz_{21}=0$, but $z_{21}$ (with $s+t=3=\max\{3,2\}$) may be nonzero; so the claimed rule 'zero if $s+t\ge\max\{n_i,n_k\}$' excludes admissible matrices. The paper's own Example exa1 allows a nonzero (1,2) entry of $Z_{12}$ with $1+2=3=\max\{3,2\}$, contradicting (gs-28). Moreover, exa1 presents $g_{12},g_{13},g_{21},g_{22},g_{31},f_{12},f_{21},\ldots$ as free parameters although the defining equations force relations such as $ag_{13}+bg_{22}=0$, $ag_{22}+bg_{31}=0$ and $af_{12}+bf_{21}=0$; the displayed family is strictly larger than $\Theta_{(a,b,j)}$, so neither the general form nor the example describes the solution set correctly.

failure_location.quote: and $Z_{ik}\in\mathbb{C}^{n_i^{(j)}\times n_k^{(j)}}$ is a matrix that the $(s,t)$-element of $Z_{ik}$ is zero if $s+t\geq\max\{n_i^{(j)}, n_k^{(j)}\}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the cross-block vanishing rule to '$(s,t)$-element zero if $s+t\ge\max\{n_i^{(j)},n_k^{(j)}\}+1$' and add the surviving shift relations; restate Example exa1's parameters subject to those relations.
issues.overall_effect: The announced canonical description of the sets $\Theta_{(a,b,j)}$, which underlies the parametrization of the Γ-blocks in Theorems thm-gamma/thm-gamma-2, is wrong; the membership statements made via the definition (gs-19) remain correct.
issues.title: Cross-block vanishing rule in the canonical form of Θ is false and contradicted by the paper's own example
issues.why_classification: A local correction of an auxiliary characterization; the theorems' Θ-membership statements use only the definition (gs-19), so every substantive claim survives after this local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let the SVD \cite{Roger-book-2012} of $W_1$ be 
 $$W_1=UD\overline{V}^T,\ \  D=\mbox{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots, \sigma_n),\ \ \sigma_j>0,$$
 where $U, V\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ are unitary matrices.

issues.failure_explanation: With $W_1=UD\overline V^{\,T}$ and $P=\mathrm{diag}(U,\overline V)$, the (1,2) block of $PWP^T$ equals $UW_1\overline V^{\,T}=U^2D(\overline V^{\,T})^2$, not $D$; the displayed congruence $PWP^T=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&D\\-\epsilon D&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ therefore does not follow and is false in general (already for $n=1$, $W_1=[\mathrm i]$: $U=1$, $V=-\mathrm i$, $P=\mathrm{diag}(1,\mathrm i)$, and $PWP^T=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\\epsilon&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]\ne\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-\epsilon&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$). The lemma's statement is nevertheless true: taking $P=\mathrm{diag}(U^H,V^T)$ (unitary) gives $PWP^T=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&D\\-\epsilon D&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ directly from the SVD, so only the proof's final step is defective.

failure_location.quote: Denote by $P=\mbox{diag}(U, \overline{V})$. It is easy to verify that (\ref{gs-30}) holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the concluding step by $P=\mathrm{diag}(U^H, V^T)$ (or cite the Autonne–Takagi factorization for $T$-even/odd forms); the statement (gs-30) then holds verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The only proof of Lemma lem-3 is invalid; Theorem thm-s-1 cites the lemma's statement (which is true), so with the one-line correction all downstream uses are restored.
issues.title: Lemma lem-3's proof verifies the wrong congruence
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction to the proof; the lemma's statement and all dependent results are preserved unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let the SVD of $S_j$ be $S_j=Q_{j1}D_jQ_{j2}^H$, where $Q_{j1}$ and $Q_{j2}$ are unitary matrices and $D_j=\mbox{diag}(\sigma_1^{(j)}, \ldots, \sigma_{n_j}^{(j)})$

issues.failure_explanation: The transform relating the parameter matrices of the pairs $(X,J)$ and $(\tilde X,J)$ with $\tilde X=XS$ is $\tilde\Gamma=S^{-1}\Gamma S^{-H}$, not the congruence $D^{-1}Q_j\Gamma_jQ_j^HD_{jj}^{-1}$ used in the proof. In Case 1, with $S_j=Q_{j1}D_jQ_{j2}^H$ and $Q_j=\mathrm{diag}(Q_{j1},Q_{j2})$, the (1,2) block of $Q_j\Gamma_jQ_j^H$ is $Q_{j1}S_jQ_{j2}^H=Q_{j1}^2D_j(Q_{j2}^H)^2$, which is not $D_j$ in general (already for $S_j=\mathrm i I$ it is not), so the displayed normalization $\tilde S_j=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&I\\-\epsilon I&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ is false; the unitary must enter as $Q_j^H(\cdot)Q_j$ (e.g. $\mathrm{diag}(Q_{j1}^H,Q_{j2})$) and the scaling must sit between the two conjugations, which is incompatible with the paper's own choice $\tilde X_j=X_jD_{jj}Q_j$. In Case 2 the same error recurs ($Q_jS_jQ_j^H=Q_j^2\Sigma_j(Q_j^H)^2\ne\Sigma_j$) and $D_{jj}=|D_j|^{1/2}$ references an undefined $D_j$. Finally, the assembly is inconsistent: for $\tilde X=XDP$ (i.e. $S=DP$) the matrix corresponding to $(\tilde X,J)$ is $S^{-1}\Gamma S^{-H}=P^HD^{-1}\Gamma D^{-1}P$, whereas the proof uses $D^{-1}P\Gamma P^HD^{-1}$; these agree only if $PD=DP$, which is neither assumed nor true in general. Hence the proof does not establish that the displayed $\tilde\Gamma$ corresponds to the claimed standard pair.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the normalization with correctly oriented conjugations: first conjugate $\Gamma_j$ by $\mathrm{diag}(Q_{j1},Q_{j2})^H(\cdot)(\mathrm{diag}(Q_{j1},Q_{j2}))$ to reach $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&D_j\\-\epsilon D_j&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$, then scale by $D_{jj}^{-1}$ on both sides, updating the pair as $\tilde X_j=X_j\,\mathrm{diag}(Q_{j1},Q_{j2})D_{jj}$ (commutation with $J_j$ holds since $J_j$ is scalar there); analogously in Case 2 with the spectral factor $Q_j$; and replace the final assembly by $\tilde\Gamma=(DP)^{-1}\Gamma(DP)^{-H}$.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm-s-2 (semi-simple H-case normalization to the form (gs-35)) is left unproven; its statement is plausibly correct but nothing in the source supports it.
issues.title: Scaling/congruence construction in the proof of Theorem thm-s-2 is invalid
issues.why_classification: The proof's core scaling step fails in both cases and must be reworked (several interlocking displayed identities), but the corrected argument is a contained, standard SVD/Takagi computation and the theorem's statement, including the advertised form (gs-35), is recoverable without new architecture or loss of the guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
if there exists a matrix  $\tilde{X}_1\in\mathbb{K}^{n\times p}$ such that $\begin{bmatrix}
\tilde{X}\\
\tilde{X}\tilde{\Lambda}\\
\end{bmatrix}$ is nonsingular
form a solution of the Problem \ref{pro-1}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives the solution from Theorem main-thm applied to the pair $(\tilde X,\tilde\Lambda)$, $\tilde X=[\tilde X_1,X_2]$, $\tilde\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\tilde\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2)$, whose hypothesis $\tilde X_L=[\tilde X;\tilde X\tilde\Lambda]$ nonsingular is stated as needed but is neither among the theorem's hypotheses nor verified for the choice $\tilde X_1=X_1\Phi$. It can fail: for $P(\lambda)=\lambda^2+1$ ($n=1$, $A=1$, $Q=0$, standard pair $X=[1,1]$, $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\mathrm i,-\mathrm i)$, $\Gamma=\mathrm{diag}(-\mathrm i/2,\,\mathrm i/2)$), take $p=1$, $\Phi=[\phi]$ with $|\phi|=1$, $\tilde\Lambda_1=[-\mathrm i]$, $\tilde\Gamma_1=[-\mathrm i/2]$. All stated hypotheses hold ($\sigma(\Lambda_1)\cap\sigma(\Lambda_2^{-\star})=\emptyset$, $\sigma(\Lambda_1)\cap\sigma(\tilde\Lambda_1)=\emptyset$, and $\Phi\tilde\Gamma_1\Phi^H=-\mathrm i/2=\Gamma_1$), yet $\tilde X_L=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}\phi&1\\-\mathrm i\phi&-\mathrm i\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ is singular ($\det=-\mathrm i\phi+\mathrm i\phi=0$) and the formula (gg-10-1) gives $\tilde A^{-1}=1-\tfrac12-\tfrac12=0$, so $\tilde A$ does not exist and no solution of Problem pro-1 is produced.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $[\tilde X;\ \tilde X\tilde\Lambda]$ with $\tilde X=[X_1\Phi, X_2]$ is nonsingular (e.g. $\sigma(\tilde\Lambda_1)\cap\sigma(\Lambda_2)=\emptyset$ with the usual genericity); under it the proof applies verbatim and every advertised guarantee survives.
issues.overall_effect: The no-spill-over guarantee of Theorem thm-eep fails for admissible data whose prescribed new eigenvalue coincides with a kept eigenvalue; the claimed solution may be undefined.
issues.title: Theorem thm-eep lacks the nonsingularity hypothesis its proof needs
issues.why_classification: Imposing one additional standard spectral-separation/local hypothesis repairs the theorem completely; the construction, formulas and the no-spill-over guarantee are unchanged.
